response.justification: Experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map, FOSS4G talk) and some high-throughput, low-latency backend work at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby. However, the core requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) development — is essentially absent: the only C/C++ exposure is a six-month stint at National Instruments in 2014-2015 and a university thesis project, with no Rust at all. The last decade has been dominated by TypeScript/Node.js, D, and web/full-stack product work, so there is little evidence of the systems-level pipeline engineering, distributed-systems depth, or navigation/routing quality assurance the role demands. Worth a conversation only if the team is open to a strong generalist ramping up on C++.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS platform experience, including an open-source mapping product
Low-latency, high-volume microservices experience (millions of req/s at Sociomantic)
Broad polyglot background with strong testing/TDD and Linux/DevOps fundamentals
concerns: Modern C++ experience is ~6 months and over a decade old; no Rust
No navigation/routing tile pipeline or map data transformation experience
Recent roles are web/full-stack TypeScript, not systems or data-pipeline engineering
